turns.input: Bram Kessel gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration:
Bram Kessel reached down and lifted the pair of worn leather boots from where they'd been sitting beside his feet, holding them out toward Nicco with both hands. "Found these in the back of my dry storage," he said, his booming voice carrying across the modest bustle of Heartstone Square. "Wrong size for me, wrong size for the wife, and they've sat there collecting flour dust for a season. Take them if they'll fit—you're a tall man, might do."

He stood waiting, boots extended, flour-dusted apron catching the daylight, that familiar piece of charcoal tucked behind his ear.

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Bram Kessel's eyebrows rise, but he keeps his hands at his sides. "You're sure? They're decent leather, not cracked, soles still good." He eyes Nicco's feet with brief assessment. "Well. Suit yourself. Back they go to the flour dust, then." He tucks the boots under one arm without further argument, already glancing toward the street with the restless energy of a man who has deliveries to coordinate.

The afternoon light falls flat across Heartstone Square, and the tavern sign of The Coined Lie creaks on its hinge somewhere behind them.
